assertions.assertion: If no committed matching shared-slot generation exists when an occurrence performs its shared probe, the shared exact cache cannot supply that occurrence's exact result.
supports: shared cache begins invocation-local and has no cross-invocation persistence
assertions.scope: shared exact cache only; local exact cache is separate

assertions.assertion: A shared publication cannot reduce the producer occurrence's already-completed exact-resolution work; its possible reuse benefit begins only with later occurrences after commit.
supports: exact result is established before local publication
private exact store precedes optional shared-store attempt
shared readers require a committed generation

assertions.assertion: For a committed shared exact fact, the reuse opportunity window is bounded after commit and before invocation teardown.
supports: shared cache lifetime is one solve invocation
cache is created for invocation and disappears at teardown

assertions.assertion: The current shared exact-cache protocol cannot coordinate same-q_r resolution occurrences that are already active before the first matching exact commit, because it represents store state but no search-in-flight ownership/state.
supports: shared hits require committed matching exact facts

assertions.assertion: Within one exact q_r key, current share eligibility is occurrence-blind: worker, alpha/beta window, route, timing and already-paid work cannot alter the share decision.
supports: fixed key/mask/hash gives the same share decision for all workers

assertions.assertion: Winner arbitration selects a completed exact-result occurrence; it does not create the result's exactness.
supports: worker publishes exact result and completion before winner CAS

assertions.assertion: Lazy SMP duplicate-work coordination has two structurally distinct temporal phases relative to the first committed exact fact for a key: pre-commit duplicate resolution and post-commit exact-value reuse.
A mechanism confined to committed-row residency/replacement can change post-commit reuse but cannot eliminate same-key work already underway in the pre-commit phase.

The current key-hash sharing gate cannot express transition-selective treatment among different occurrences of the same q_r state; any such selection requires additional occurrence/transition information or a different boundary.
For the measured production workloads, the post-commit shared exact-cache channel is empirically a cross-worker CPC_EXACT memoizer.
supports: PROVENANCE_CENSUS_0_1: 100% of committed shared stores and consumed hits are CPC_EXACT

assertions.assertion: Route-6/8 protected residency acts only on the post-commit phase; it cannot alter the pre-commit overlap class measured by the overlap census.
The measured Lazy SMP sharing problem contains at least two independent optimization regimes: pre-commit overlap and post-commit CPC-exact residency/reuse.
Raw shared-hit count is incomplete telemetry for total cross-worker duplicate-resolution opportunity because pre-commit overlapping same-q_r work produces no shared hit by construction.
A positive route-residency A/B result is evidence only about post-commit reuse economics and cannot, by itself, validate or falsify an in-flight duplicate-suppression mechanism.
Any optimization restricted to the current direct-mapped committed exact-cache state machine has a structural ceiling: it cannot remove first-wave same-key overlap before an exact fact is committed.
